$comment: Compatibility manifest for the controlled downgrade (see the controlled-downgrade conception, lot A).
The CLI READS this file and never infers compatibility from a version number, so a release that is
not described here can only ever be told to restore from a backup -- which is the safe direction.
THREE targets are offered, all measured: 1.6.16 (the newest stable 1.6 release, published 2026-10-14), 1.6.15 (published
2026-09-21) and 1.6.14. A pair is looked up on (from, to, engine), so `bwcli plugin backup downgrade 1.6.16`,
`... 1.6.15` and `... 1.6.14` each pick their own row. 1.6.16 is the shortest path -- two revisions (the 1.7.0~alpha head and
1.6.17~rc1) instead of eight to 1.6.15 and twelve to 1.6.14 -- and the one to prefer; see the notes on the 1.6.14 rows for what the extra revisions cost.
'from' is matched against /usr/share/bunkerweb/VERSION verbatim. BUMP IT WITH src/VERSION: a stale
'from' makes every pair unmatched and pins the product to restore_only. tests/unit/backup/
test_downgrade_manifest.py fails when the two disagree, so the bump cannot be forgotten silently.
MEASURED, per engine, by an executed upgrade+downgrade: `mode`, `data_loss`, every `fingerprint`
field, and each `restore_only` reason. The main run carries sentinel data; the same probe is also re-run with NO sentinel
rows, so a structural blocker is measured even where a data-dependent one would abort first. Each reason names the artefact it was read from.
built from `git show v<target>:src/common/db/model.py`, seeded, upgraded to the 1.7 head, seeded again
with 1.7-only rows and then downgraded back. 1.6.14: .cache/results-2026-09-06-wave13/report-DG-AD.md
and dgad-probe-*.json. 1.6.15: .cache/wave21-2026-09-21/report-DG-1615.md and dg1615-probe-*.json.
`generated_at` is the date of the most recent measurement in this file, which is what the staleness
guard in tests/unit/backup/test_downgrade_manifest.py compares against the head's Create Date. It is NOT
a claim that every row was re-taken on that date: the 1.6.14 fingerprints are wave 13's (2026-09-06),
re-confirmed on the post-1.6.16~rc1 chain for the landing revision and version on SQLITE ONLY (dg1615-drafts-1614.json); the other three engines' 1.6.14 fingerprints were NOT re-run this wave.
The 1.6.15 rows were measured on all four engines on 2026-09-21. On 2026-09-25 the 1.7 heads were regenerated as 1.7.0~alpha and the same probe was
re-run against them for both targets on all four engines (regen-probe-*.json, lane REGEN): sqlite and postgresql are reversible with outcomes
identical to 2026-09-21, and mariadb/mysql abort on the error-1553 blocker alone, with or without sentinel rows.
On 2026-10-05 the heads were regenerated again, on top of 1.6.16~rc2 (the METRICS_REDIS_TTL normalisation) and 1.6.16~rc3 (the bw_blob_chunks table), and the same probe was
re-run for both targets on all four engines (sqlite, PostgreSQL, MariaDB 11, MySQL 8.4; with and without sentinel rows): the outcomes did not move -- sqlite and postgresql reversible,
mariadb/mysql abort on the error-1553 blocker -- but two figures did: the 1.7-only table count (bw_blob_chunks) and the version a failed attempt leaves in bw_metadata (1.6.16~rc3).
A third run set one bw_plugins row to the new `download` method before the downgrade: sqlite and postgresql ran to completion and left a schema 1.6.x cannot read (SELECT on bw_plugins
raises LookupError on the unknown label), mariadb/mysql aborted on error 1265. The preflight therefore answers restore_only while any `download` plugin or any bw_blob_chunks row exists (checks
`download_plugins` and `irrepresentable_data`); no conversion is offered. Probe, logs and JSON: .cache/wave24-2026-10-05/proofs/L4c/probe/.
On 2026-10-14 the heads were regenerated a third time, on top of 1.6.16~rc4 and the final 1.6.16 (both only set bw_metadata.version and clear last_pro_check; no schema operation), and the same probe

was re-run for both targets and the `download` row run on all four engines (sqlite, PostgreSQL 16, MariaDB 11, MySQL 8.4; with and without sentinel rows). The outcomes did not move: sqlite and postgresql
reversible, mariadb/mysql abort on the error-1553 blocker, the `download` row still ends in a schema 1.6.x cannot read (sqlite/postgresql) or error 1265 (mariadb/mysql). What moved: the head ids, the

number of revisions the path runs (seven to 1.6.15, eleven to 1.6.14: 1.6.16 and 1.6.16~rc4 are new), and the version a failed attempt leaves in bw_metadata (now 1.6.16). The 14 leftover 1.7 tables and
the empty list of missing tables of a failed mariadb/mysql attempt were measured again and are unchanged. Probe, logs and JSON: .cache/wave24-2026-10-05/proofs/L4d/probe/.
On 2026-10-15 the heads were regenerated a fourth time, on top of dev's 1.6.17~rc1 (it only sets bw_metadata.version and clears last_pro_check; no schema operation), and the same probe

was re-run for both targets and the `download` row run on all four engines (sqlite, PostgreSQL 16, MariaDB 11, MySQL 8.4.11; with and without sentinel rows). The outcomes did not move: sqlite and postgresql
reversible, mariadb/mysql abort on the error-1553 blocker, the `download` row still ends in a schema 1.6.x cannot read (sqlite/postgresql) or error 1265 (mariadb/mysql). What moved: the head ids, the
number of revisions the path runs (eight to 1.6.15, twelve to 1.6.14: 1.6.17~rc1 is new), and the version a failed attempt leaves in bw_metadata (now 1.6.17~rc1). The 14 leftover 1.7 tables and
the empty list of missing tables of a failed mariadb/mysql attempt were measured again and are unchanged. Probe, logs and JSON: .cache/wave25-2026-10-15/proofs/W25-D5/probe/.

On 2026-10-16 the 1.6.16 target was added (PO decision D21; no Alembic revision was created or edited: the chain already carries the 1.6.16 revision of every engine). Its four pairs were measured with the same probe, started

from the real 1.6.16 install instead of 1.6.15 (the model of tag v1.6.16, create_all, stamped at the 1.6.16 revision, seeded, upgraded to the 1.7.0~alpha head, seeded again with 1.7-only rows, downgraded to the 1.6.16

revision), on all four engines (sqlite, PostgreSQL 16, MariaDB 11, MySQL 8.4.11; with and without sentinel rows, plus the `download` row). The outcomes match the 1.6.15 pairs: sqlite and postgresql reversible with an empty

schema diff and bw_metadata.version = 1.6.16 afterwards, mariadb/mysql abort on the error-1553 blocker (error 1265 first when a `download` row exists) and leave bw_metadata.version at 1.6.17~rc1. Three figures are specific

to this target: the path runs two revisions, bw_blob_chunks is part of the target schema and its row survives the downgrade on all four engines (the 1.6.15 and 1.6.14 paths drop the table), and a failed mariadb/mysql

attempt leaves 13 tables from 1.7 (14 on the 1.6.15 path, which counts bw_blob_chunks among them). The 1.6.15 and 1.6.14 rows were not re-run. Probe, logs and JSON: .cache/wave26-2026-10-16/proofs/W26-DG/probe/.
DERIVED, not measured: the `artifacts` map. It comes from reading the tree (src/common/helpers/data.sh
is byte-identical between v1.6.14, v1.6.15, v1.6.16 and 1.7, so the /data layout cannot have moved) and from what
each job regenerates, not from a downgrade run. Treat those values as a documented expectation.
`setting_drafts` says what the path does to individual setting drafts (is_draft = 1 on bw_global_values or
bw_services_settings): "kept" when the target still declares the flag (1.6.15 and 1.6.16), "refused" when the path runs
1.6.15~rc3's downgrade(), which refuses while a draft row exists. The preflight counts the drafts and refuses
the same way; a row without the field is treated as unproven (restore_only) whenever drafts exist.

fingerprint.method: 1.6.14 create_all -> stamp -> sentinel rows -> alembic upgrade head -> 1.7-only sentinel rows -> alembic downgrade to 1.6.14 (twelve revisions run: the 1.7.0~alpha head, 1.6.17~rc1, 1.6.16, 1.6.16~rc4, 1.6.16~rc3, 1.6.16~rc2, the METRICS_REDIS_TTL normalisation, 1.6.16~rc1, 1.6.15, 1.6.15~rc3, 1.6.15~rc2, 1.6.15~rc1)
fingerprint.baseline_row_delta_explained: +1: bw_ui_user_preferences is renamed back into bw_ui_user_columns_preferences rather than dropped
fingerprint.target_model_select_failures_detail: bw_ui_user_columns_preferences raised JSONDecodeError. An artifact of the probe's own sentinel, which wrote a non-JSON string into bw_ui_user_preferences.value before the downgrade renamed the table; real 1.7 preference values are JSON documents. The renamed-back rows still reach 1.6.14 as the wrong KIND of preference -- see the note below.

notes: Every table and column the 1.6.14 model declares is present after the downgrade, with no extras.

Non-column user preferences (theme_mode, whats_new, onboarding, walkthrough) reappear in 1.6.14 as bogus per-table column layouts: the downgrade renames bw_ui_user_preferences to bw_ui_user_columns_preferences wholesale instead of filtering the column-layout keys. Expected to be cosmetic rather than a crash, because every writer in src/ui/app/routes/ stores a JSON document -- but that is read off the callers, NOT measured: the probe's own sentinel was not JSON and did raise JSONDecodeError through the 1.6.14 model.

MEASURED 2026-09-21 on SQLite (dg1615-drafts-1614.json), and NOT reflected in `mode`. Engine-independent by construction: the refusal is a Python RuntimeError raised inside the migration, before any DDL is emitted, and the four engines' 1.6.15~rc3 revisions are byte-identical Python. It is since the 1.6.15/1.6.16~rc1 chain landed, this path runs 1.6.15~rc3's downgrade(), which REFUSES with "Cannot downgrade individual setting drafts while bw_global_values contains draft rows" when bw_global_values or bw_services_settings still holds is_draft = 1 -- dropping the flag would silently activate the retained value. The run then stops stamped at the 1.6.15~rc3 revision with bw_metadata.version = '1.6.15~rc3'; `bwcli plugin backup downgrade --execute` catches that and restores its own pre-downgrade backup, so nothing is lost -- but the preflight now refuses before that point: it counts the draft rows, and this row's setting_drafts is "refused". 1.7 creates and clears individual setting drafts itself (the RAW editor, PUT /global_settings/config draft_settings), and an upgrade from 1.6.15~rc3 or later carries them over, so any installation can hold them. Activate or delete them before a downgrade to 1.6.14; the 1.6.15 target stops above that revision and keeps them -- prefer it.

notes: Two enum TYPES the 1.7 upgrade creates are not dropped by the downgrade (instance_tls_mode_enum, resource_kinds_enum), and the values added to api_resource_enum and settings_types_enum cannot be removed at all -- PostgreSQL has no ALTER TYPE ... DROP VALUE. Measured harmless: 1.6.14 never references them, the one SELECT failure the probe recorded is its own non-JSON sentinel (see target_model_select_failures_detail) and not these types, and a later re-upgrade is idempotent (CREATE TYPE ... Those leftover values are also what SAVES PostgreSQL where MariaDB/MySQL fail: bw_ui_users.method keeps 'api' as a legal label instead of having the enum narrowed under it.

releases.reason: The 1.7 head's downgrade() does not run to completion on MariaDB. One blocker, structural and data-independent, MEASURED 2026-10-15 on the regenerated 1.7.0~alpha head, with and without sentinel rows (.cache/wave25-2026-10-15/proofs/W25-D5/probe/probe-1.6.14-mariadb.json, probe-1.6.14-empty-mariadb.json): DROP INDEX ix_bw_resource_group_usages_plugin_id fails with error 1553, 'needed in a foreign key constraint', on an index drop_table makes redundant. The abort is inside the 1.7 head's own downgrade(), which both targets execute in full. The former data-dependent blocker, error 1265 on ALTER TABLE bw_ui_users MODIFY method ENUM(...) for a row holding 'api', is gone: 1.6.15~rc2 already adds 'api' to method and its downgrade() keeps it, so the regenerated head no longer narrows the column (the same probe, with an 'api' row, now gets past it). Worse than a plain refusal: the failure is partial. The first statement of downgrade() commits the bw_metadata version bump under MariaDB's non-transactional DDL, so a failed attempt leaves bw_metadata.version at 1.6.17~rc1 while alembic_version still names the 1.7 head and the schema is a hybrid -- a state the preflight refuses and the scheduler entrypoint cannot recover from. Restore from backup is the only path. A plugin row labelled `download` (the label the 1.7.0~alpha head adds) brings a 1265 class back: with one present the narrowing MODIFY of bw_plugins.method fails with error 1265 before the 1553 above (MEASURED 2026-10-15, probe-1.6.15-download-*.json); the preflight refuses such an installation before it gets that far.

fingerprint.method: same probe as sqlite/postgresql; the downgrade aborted mid-way

The shortest rollback: this path runs two revisions, the 1.7.0~alpha head and 1.6.17~rc1 (which only records the version), against eight to 1.6.15 and twelve to 1.6.14. It stops above 1.6.16~rc1 to 1.6.16, so it reaches none of the revisions the 1.6.15 and 1.6.14 targets run: the model of tag v1.6.16 is the 1.6.15 model plus the bw_blob_chunks table and a version default, and the columns bw_ui_users.totp_last_counter and the is_draft flags survive here as they do on the 1.6.15 target. data_loss_detail.columns is the union for the 1.6.14 target and therefore over-states bw_ui_users for this pair by that one column.

bw_blob_chunks belongs to the 1.6.16 schema (added by 1.6.16~rc3), so unlike the 1.6.15 and 1.6.14 targets this path does not drop it: the probe seeded one chunk row before the upgrade and found it after the downgrade, on all four engines (1 -> 1). The probe's chunk row has no owner row behind it, so what is measured is the table and its rows, not a chunked value. The preflight does not know that: it counts bw_blob_chunks and answers restore_only while a row exists, whatever the target, so it is stricter than this target needs (the safe direction). Whether a 1.6.16 reader reassembles a chunked value after the round trip is NOT measured here.

Non-column user preferences (theme_mode, whats_new, onboarding, walkthrough) reappear in 1.6.16 as bogus per-table column layouts: the downgrade renames bw_ui_user_preferences to bw_ui_user_columns_preferences wholesale instead of filtering the column-layout keys. notes: Every table and column the 1.6.16 model declares is present after the downgrade, with no extras (schema_diff empty, with and without sentinel rows). 1.7 adds fifteen tables to the 1.6.16 schema; all fifteen are gone afterwards.

Two enum TYPES the 1.7 upgrade creates are still not dropped (instance_tls_mode_enum, resource_kinds_enum) and the values added to api_resource_enum and settings_types_enum cannot be removed at all. Measured here against 1.6.16's own model: the same two orphans, no SELECT failure caused by them.
Those leftover values are also what SAVES PostgreSQL where MariaDB/MySQL fail: bw_ui_users.method keeps 'api' as a legal label instead of having the enum narrowed under it.

The shortest rollback: this path runs two revisions, the 1.7.0~alpha head and 1.6.17~rc1 (which only records the version), against eight to 1.6.15 and twelve to 1.6.14. It stops above 1.6.16~rc1 to 1.6.16, so it reaches none of the revisions the 1.6.15 and 1.6.14 targets run: the model of tag v1.6.16 is the 1.6.15 model plus the bw_blob_chunks table and a version default, and the columns bw_ui_users.totp_last_counter and the is_draft flags survive here as they do on the 1.6.15 target. data_loss_detail.columns is the union for the 1.6.14 target and therefore over-states bw_ui_users for this pair by that one column.

bw_blob_chunks belongs to the 1.6.16 schema (added by 1.6.16~rc3), so unlike the 1.6.15 and 1.6.14 targets this path does not drop it: the probe seeded one chunk row before the upgrade and found it after the downgrade, on all four engines (1 -> 1). The probe's chunk row has no owner row behind it, so what is measured is the table and its rows, not a chunked value. The preflight does not know that: it counts bw_blob_chunks and answers restore_only while a row exists, whatever the target, so it is stricter than this target needs (the safe direction). Whether a 1.6.16 reader reassembles a chunked value after the round trip is NOT measured here.

Non-column user preferences (theme_mode, whats_new, onboarding, walkthrough) reappear in 1.6.16 as bogus per-table column layouts: the downgrade renames bw_ui_user_preferences to bw_ui_user_columns_preferences wholesale instead of filtering the column-layout keys. Expected to be cosmetic rather than a crash, because every writer in src/ui/app/routes/ stores a JSON document -- but that is read off the callers, NOT measured: the probe's own sentinel was not JSON and did raise JSONDecodeError through the 1.6.16 model.

data_loss_detail.$comment: Applies to every in_place_tested pair above. 'certain' = the rows are destroyed and cannot be recreated; 'conditional' = destroyed but regenerable, with a stated cost. The preflight counts the live rows and compares them against this map.

why.bw_bans: regenerable by the sync-bans job, which relearns from the instances' shared dicts and Redis; ban durations and tombstones are lost
why.bw_blob_chunks: the pieces of every plugin archive, plugin page and job cache stored in chunks (MySQL/MariaDB when larger than one statement can carry; any engine when the content begins with the bytes BunkerWeb uses to flag a chunked value); the owner row keeps an 80-byte marker, so dropping the table leaves the owners pointing at nothing. Counted by the preflight, which answers restore_only while any row exists; plugins labelled `download` are refused by their own check
why.bw_ui_user_preferences: renamed back into bw_ui_user_columns_preferences rather than dropped, so the rows survive; only their meaning is lost (every key becomes a per-table column layout)
why.bw_ui_user_webauthn_credentials: every registered passkey; a passkey-only user must fall back to password + TOTP
why.bw_certificates: every centrally stored certificate and private key
why.bw_metrics_requests: all request metrics and the threat map history
why.bw_resources: every attachable resource, and by foreign key the redirects, upstream pools, workflows and resource groups keyed on it

data_loss_detail.columns_why: Dropped by the downgrade on every engine, on the way to 1.6.14. The bw_instances credential and enrolment columns matter most: every enrolled instance has to be re-registered against the global API_TOKEN after a rollback. Three entries are target-dependent: bw_ui_users.totp_last_counter is dropped by 1.6.15~rc2's downgrade and the is_draft flag on bw_global_values and bw_services_settings by 1.6.15~rc3's, and the 1.6.15 target reaches neither, so a rollback to 1.6.15 keeps all three. This map is the union, so it never under-states a loss; it over-states those three columns for the 1.6.15 pairs. Dropping is_draft is never silent: 1.6.15~rc3's downgrade refuses while a draft row exists, and so does the preflight (see each row's setting_drafts).

not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_metrics_baseline: observability, not configuration, and always non-empty -- counting it would pin every installation to restore_only forever
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_ui_user_preferences: every UI user has rows here (theme, dismissed notices, onboarding progress, what's-new stamps, column layouts), so counting it would pin every installation to restore_only. Not destroyed outright: the downgrade renames the table back to bw_ui_user_columns_preferences, so the rows survive and only their meaning is lost
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_resource_attachments: covered transitively: every row keys on bw_resources, which IS counted, so this table is empty whenever that one is
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_resource_group_entries: covered transitively: an entry keys on a group, and the operator-built groups ARE counted (bw_resource_groups WHERE plugin_id IS NULL). A seeded group cannot be given operator entries either -- update_resource_group refuses when method is not editable -- so what is left here is re-seeded by the next upgrade
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_resource_group_usages: a usage row is the index of which plugin consumes which group; it is rebuilt from the settings that reference the group, and those settings are 1.6.x rows the downgrade keeps. Not empty when a seeded group is in use, which is why it is not counted
not_counted_by_the_preflight.bw_upstream_servers: covered transitively: every row keys on bw_upstreams, which IS counted
